title: Openness of the very-tame locus
statement: Let $(Y,M)$ be a separated locally Noetherian fs log regular scheme [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] with an action of a finite group $H$ by log automorphisms [def-per-fs-log-group-action]. Define $T\subseteq |Y|$ to be the set of points $y$ such that for every geometric point $\bar y$ above $y$, its inertia has order invertible in the residue field and acts trivially on both $M_{\bar y}/\mathcal O_{Y,\bar y}^\times$ and $\operatorname{Spec}(\mathcal O_{Y,\bar y}/I_{\bar y})$, where $I_{\bar y}$ is generated by the images of nonunit log sections [def-per-very-tame-fs-log-action]. Then $T$ is an $H$-invariant open subset. For a strict $H$-equivariant etale morphism $v:(Y',M')\to(Y,M)$ which induces isomorphisms of geometric inertia groups, $Y'$ is fs log regular and its very-tame locus is $v^{-1}(T)$. Here strict means that $M'$ is the pullback log structure [def-trf-log-ideal-chart-presentation]; etale and geometric point have the meanings of [def-weil-etale-morphism], [def-weil-geometric-point]. Separated means that the structural morphism to $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ has closed diagonal [def-weil-proper-morphism]. No separatedness of $Y\prime$ is needed for the strict inert pullback assertion.

source.place: VI Corollary 3.6, printed p.74, and VIII Lemma 5.3.2(i), printed p.123. Strict inert etale invariance uses the same strict-local conditions in VI 3.1.

proof.text: First consider any strict equivariant etale map $v:Y'\to Y$ inducing isomorphisms of geometric inertia. Its source is locally Noetherian: choose affine charts over a Noetherian affine cover of $Y$; etaleness gives finite-presentation, hence finite-type, ring maps, and apply lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian. Pulling back fs charts gives fs charts on $Y'$. At $\bar y'$ with $\bar y=v\bar y'$, lem-trf-ind-etale-strict-local-invariance identifies the strict local rings. Strictness identifies the log stalks and their unit subgroups, and hence the characteristic monoids and nonunit ideals. Equivariance makes these identifications intertwine the specified inertia groups. Thus the regularity of the stratum and the dimension equality defining log regularity hold upstairs. The three pointwise very-tame tests agree in both directions: the inertia orders are equal, the residue fields in these strict local rings agree, and the actions on the two identified objects agree.

This proves equality of loci defined using every geometric lift, not just a chosen lift. At a point $y'$ and for each geometric $\bar y$ over $v(y')$, the precise prescribed-source-point clause of lem-weil-pbc-etale-cover-geometric-point-lift supplies a lift $\bar y'$ over $y'$ with the same algebraically closed field (apply the lemma over the open image of $v$). Therefore if all lifts over $y'$ are very tame, all lifts over $v(y')$ are; the converse follows by composition and Step 1. The same argument works for equivariance relative to an inclusion of acting groups whenever the induced geometric inertia maps are isomorphisms.

Fix $y\in T$ and choose $\bar y$ over it. Apply lem-per-pointwise-diagonal-kummer-neighbourhood. Write $L=\operatorname{Stab}_H(\bar y)$ and $K=\operatorname{Stab}_L(\bar z)$ for an arbitrary geometric point of its model $W=\operatorname{Spec}A$, where $A=B\otimes_{\Lambda[P]}\Lambda[Q]$. The integer $n=|L|$ is invertible on $W$, so $|K|$ is invertible. Every $h\in K$ multiplies each chart section $z^q$ by the unit $\chi_h(q)$ and therefore fixes its characteristic class. Since a chart generates the log structure together with units, $K$ fixes the whole characteristic monoid. No faithful character pairing is required.

For the strict-local stratum at $\bar z$, put $E=\{q\in Q:z^q(\bar z)\ne0\}$ and $J=(z^q:q\notin E)\subset A$. These are an $L$-invariant face and an $L$-stable ideal, since all monomials are eigenvectors. If $h\in K$ and $e\in E$, evaluating $h(z^e)=\chi_h(e)z^e$ at $\bar z$ gives $\chi_h(e)=1$ in its residue field. In the strict local ring a nonidentity $n$th root has unit difference from $1$, by lem-sbc-strict-local-roots-of-unity. Thus $h(z^e)=z^e$ in that ring. Put $C=\mathcal O_{W,\bar z}/I_{\bar z}$. The chart definition gives $I_{\bar z}=J\mathcal O_{W,\bar z}$. Every element of $A$ is a sum of $B$-multiples of monomials: those with exponent outside $E$ vanish in $C$, those in $E$ are fixed by the preceding root calculation, and $B$ is fixed by construction. Hence $h$ fixes the image of $A/J$ in $C$. By lem-trf-closed-immersion-strict-localization-cartesian, $C$ is the strict local ring of $\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)$ at $\bar z$. Its induced $h$-action and the identity have the same structural map to $\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)$ and the same residue embedding, since $h$ is in inertia. They agree by uniqueness in lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality. This verifies the remaining test, including nilpotents.

source.place: VI 2.3, formula (2.a) and stratum calculation; Stacks 05WS, 04GU

proof.text: Steps 3--4 apply to every geometric point of $W$, so $W$ is very tame. The model map is strict etale and identifies all geometric inertia groups, so Steps 1--2 imply that every point in its image belongs to $T$. Its image contains $y$ and is open by lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map. Taking these open images for all $y\in T$ proves openness. For $g\in H$ acting on the original scheme, $\bar y\mapsto g\bar y$ gives a bijection of geometric lifts and carries inertia to its conjugate. The log automorphism identifies their strict local rings, characteristic monoids and nonunit ideals; conjugation preserves order and the two identity-action tests. Thus $y\in T$ if and only if $gy\in T$. Together with Steps 1--2 this proves all assertions. The empty scheme or empty locus is covered by the empty union.

proof_origin.place: VI 3.5--3.7 and 2.3, VIII 5.3.2(i), with the strict inert comparison written out from the definitions.

split_report.summary: STATEMENT-DISPUTED: the original omitted separatedness; swapping the origins on the doubled affine line in characteristic 2 gives a non-open very-tame locus for the trivial log structure. Added separatedness faithfully to the global source setting. Proved strict inert invariance on strict local stalks, used one genuinely structural new pointwise diagonal Kummer model, checked all three inertia tests by explicit monomial calculation, and used open images and conjugation. No global admissibility or generic freeness was added.

lean.statement: theorem isOpen_veryTameLocus {H : Type v} [Group H] [Finite H] (Y : FineSaturatedLogScheme.{u}) (a : FSLogGroupAction H Y) [Y.scheme.IsSeparated] (hregular : Y.IsLogRegular) : IsOpen a.toEtaleLogGroupAction.veryTameLocus ∧ (∀ (g : H) (y : Y.scheme), (a.baseAction g).hom y ∈ a.toEtaleLogGroupAction.veryTameLocus ↔ y ∈ a.toEtaleLogGroupAction.veryTameLocus) ∧ ∀ (Y' : Scheme.{u}) (M' : EtaleLogStructure Y') (a' : EtaleLogGroupAction H M') (v : EtaleLogMap M' Y.logStructure), a'.IsEquivariant a.toEtaleLogGroupAction v → v.IsStrictEtale → (∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (t' : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Y') (g : H), t' ≫ (a'.baseAction g).hom = t' ↔ (t' ≫ v.base) ≫ (a.baseAction g).hom = t' ≫ v.base) → ∃ (hln : IsLocallyNoetherian Y') (hfs : M'.IsFineSaturated), (FineSaturatedLogScheme.mk Y' hln M' hfs).IsLogRegular ∧ a'.veryTameLocus = Set.preimage (fun x : Y' ↦ v.base x) a.toEtaleLogGroupAction.veryTameLocus
